summary.headline: Monte Carlo Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.51% to Rs 262 crore, but PAT fell to Rs 1.17 crore as raw-material costs rose; H1 posted a Rs 22.25 crore loss.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 262 crore (up 5.51% YoY) with operating EBITDA of Rs 28.35 crore (10.80% margin) and PAT of Rs 1.17 crore. H1 revenue was Rs 411 crore (up 6.25%), operating EBITDA Rs 15.42 crore (3.7% margin) and a loss after tax of Rs 22.25 crore. Management attributed the weakness to higher material cost, lower other income, higher employee cost and early discounting to clear old inventory, and said the timing of festive demand and retailer returns distorts the half-year. Guidance was held at low double-digit revenue growth, 40-45 new EBOs and about 20% home textile growth, with EBITDA margin now guided at plus or minus 100 bps of last year.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 35 crore in H1 FY26; about 12% of revenue vs 9% last year

segments.name: Cotton apparel
segments.commentary: Gross sales rose from Rs 326 crore in H1 FY26 to Rs 390 crore in H1 FY27; cotton is about 63% of H1 gross product sales. Jackets within cotton are a winter product.

segments.name: Home textiles
segments.commentary: Gross sales rose from Rs 83 crore to Rs 91.6 crore in H1 (about 10% growth). Management guides about 20% growth for the full year.

segments.name: Kids wear
segments.commentary: Gross sales rose from Rs 30 crore to Rs 34.5 crore in H1.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Gross sales rose from Rs 4.9 crore to Rs 9.3 crore in H1 from a small base.

segments.name: Woollen
segments.commentary: Gross sales declined from about Rs 106 crore to about Rs 94 crore in H1. Woollen is made fully in-house and is the key Q3 category.

segments.name: Solar subsidiary (new)
segments.commentary: 35 MW plant in Madhya Pradesh across three sites with PPAs signed; COD targeted 31 March 2027. Management expects about Rs 17-18 crore revenue in FY28 at 80%+ EBITDA margin and a 17-18% ROI.

guidance_outlook: Low double-digit revenue growth for FY27 reiterated; management cited about 15% growth last year.
EBITDA and PAT margin expected to be within plus or minus 100 bps of FY26, depending on Q3 performance.
Q3 expected to be better YoY, though management declined to quantify it; Q2 and Q3 are not comparable quarter-on-quarter.
Like-to-like (EBO) growth of about 9-10% expected for FY27 after about 9% in H1 and 10% last year.
40-45 new EBOs in FY27, focused on West and South; 20% home textile growth targeted.
Rebates and discounts expected up to about 10% of total for the year in one answer and 3-4% in another; the two statements conflict.
capex_capacity: Solar: 35 MW plant in Madhya Pradesh across three sites; land identified and aggregated; PPAs signed; COD targeted 31 March 2027 and management says it is on track.
Store base as of 26 September: 506 EBOs (497 a year earlier), 632 shop-in-shops (578), 1,413 MBOs (1,615), 846 national chain stores (891).
EBO economics: about Rs 12,000 per sq ft currently; aspiration to reach Rs 15,000 per sq ft in 2-3 years.
Manufacturing: about 20% of garments are made in-house (mainly t-shirts and thermals); cotton is otherwise outsourced, and management has no plans for new cotton capex.
Working capital days improved from 176 in FY25 to 146 in FY26. Debt rises seasonally at 30 September; about Rs 200 crore permanent working capital is cited for 31 March.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 8-9% taken for winter 2026 to offset raw-material inflation; management says Q3 is protected because the hike is already in place.
Cost of goods rose about 3% YoY per management, in line with its 2-3% impact estimate; pure wool raw material up about 20% YoY and expected to rise again.
Winter demand: November and December normally make up 80-85% of winter revenue; management said the season has started but gave no quantified Q3 momentum.
Festival timing: Diwali moved from October last year to November this year, shifting part of dispatches and sell-through into Q3.
Discounts rose because end-of-season sales started early, macro conditions were weak, and old inventory was liquidated; a lot sale of older stock was also executed in Q2.
West and South together were about 9.7% of gross sales; online and some other sales are not attributed to states.

qa_highlights.question: How much has RM inflation affected margins and what price increases have been taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflation raised material costs in Q2, and Q3 is protected by a winter price rise of about 8-9%. Management said the hike should be sufficient for winter wear raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why have rebates risen about 40-70% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: R.K. Sharma said rebates are 12% of revenue vs 9% last year and about 4% higher for H1. Sandeep Jain said Q2 should not be used as an annual benchmark and cited early end-of-season sales and inventory clearance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guidance for PAT and EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA and PAT margins will be within plus or minus 100 bps of last year's levels, depending on Q3. Management also said that a 20% EBITDA margin including other income is sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What are the solar subsidiary timelines and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: PPAs are signed for three sites totalling 35 MW in Madhya Pradesh with COD on 31 March 2027. Management expects about Rs 17-18 crore of FY28 revenue, with EBITDA margins above 80% and a 17-18% ROI.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Monte Carlo keep returns and sales volatility across quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Rishabh Oswal said dispatches happen in Q3 and returns come back in later quarters, so the pattern should even out as other quarters contribute more. R.K. Sharma said returns are provided for each quarter, with only marginal additional returns.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for a buyback, exports or rental models?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback discussion has taken place, and management will inform exchanges if that changes. Exports are not a priority and white-labelling is ruled out. Management has no plans to enter the rental model.

risks_watch: Margin: Q3 must deliver to hold plus or minus 100 bps of FY26 margin; H1 EBITDA margin of 3.7% leaves little room.
Net debt rose: management said FY26 year-end debt was about Rs 200 crore, while the Q2 seasonal position was about Rs 300 crore. Lease liabilities rose from Rs 129 crore (FY23) to Rs 252 crore.
Returns and old-inventory liquidation: return ratio is 30.70% in H1 and management says there is an SOP to clear old stock within a set period.
Like-to-like growth and store productivity: EBO LFL is about 9% for H1, but total revenue growth is about 5-6% and the EBO expansion plan (40-45 stores) depends on economic conditions.
Solar project: COD 31 March 2027; revenue guidance was given inconsistently (a range of plus or minus 5%, and Rs 17-18 crore).
Rebates and discounts: guidance for the full year is inconsistent, with up to 10% of total in one answer and 3-4% in another.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and the Q3 festive season, but defensive on Q2 losses, margins, returns and the solar diversion. Management repeatedly deferred to Q3 and used "plus or minus 100 bps" language, and it declined to quantify festival-shift and inventory impacts.
key_quotes: Please don't judge us on the basis of just one quarter alone. Please judge us on the basis of annual performance.
It is a one-off investment and it should be treated like one.
We expect a ROI of 17%-18%. Yes, but we will send you the exact details over mail.
Quarter-on-quarter, quarter 2 and quarter 3 are not comparable. So it is a year-on-year commentary that we are giving on quarter 3.

adds.what: 35 MW solar plant in Madhya Pradesh (solar subsidiary, three sites, PPAs signed)
40-45 new EBOs in FY27 (focused on West and South)

growth.why: Low double-digit FY27 revenue growth (midpoint ~10%) is held, backed by a 8-9% winter price hike, 40-45 new EBOs and ~9-10% like-to-like growth, but H1 revenue grew only 6.25% and no quantified Q3 momentum was given, so backing is partial.
